evals.prompt: Use Plan mode for our existing GitHub Enterprise Cloud account `contoso` on github.com. We want a new organization called `contoso-payments` for about 45 engineers. It needs platform, backend, and frontend teams; a private service repository created from our golden template; read-only Actions tokens; CodeQL and secret scanning; and Copilot for the backend and frontend teams. Assess the live account first. Do not make changes yet.
evals.expected_output: The skill verifies the active GitHub CLI identity, performs progressive read-only discovery, proposes a capability checklist, and carries safe recommended defaults into the review-only plan. It asks only for material choices that lack a safe default and does not run writes.
expectations: The response does not run or recommend running a mutating GitHub command before a reviewed plan and explicit approval.
The response verifies or attempts to verify the active GitHub host, actor, enterprise access, and target organization state before planning.
The response proposes a capability checklist covering organization, teams, repository template, Actions, security, and Copilot without asking for checklist approval.
The response asks only about a material choice that lacks a safe default; otherwise it carries recommended values into the plan.
The response treats Copilot seat assignment as a separate billing-sensitive change with named recipients or teams.
The response distinguishes observed settings from effective policy source or inherited enterprise constraints.
Any executable plan operation records an exact official endpoint documentation URL and check timestamp, supported API version, host, token type, permissions, and availability.
The response labels recommendations by source and keeps customer decisions distinct from recommendations.

It distinguishes configured grants from effective access, plans additions before removals, classifies removals as high impact, and includes every write in one explicit execution approval.
expectations: The response does not remove access or run any mutating GitHub command in the one-shot evaluation.
The response assesses organization base permissions, team hierarchy or inheritance, team repository grants, direct collaborators, and selected repository visibility before proposing removals.
The response distinguishes configured grants from each person's effective repository access.
The response requires an exact before-and-after access list and a recovery path before any removal batch.
The response classifies access removals as high impact and separates additions or corrective grants from removals.
The response defines one execution approval covering the exact eligible batches and their acceptance checks.

evals.prompt: Offline Assess tabletop only for enterprise `contoso` on github.com and organization `contoso-engineering`; do not contact GitHub or inspect real credentials. Check ownership continuity and Actions workflow-token defaults. Supplied read evidence at 2026-10-12T08:00:00Z verifies the intended actor and target, two active organization owners, and organization default_workflow_permissions=write with no enforced enterprise override. Supplied official guidance review says restricted read-only workflow-token defaults are recommended; its reference is https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#modifying-the-permissions-for-the-github_token. The agreed assessment baseline is read-only defaults. Owner recovery readiness could not be verified because the relevant read was denied; record insufficient_permission and ask the responsible owner to provide recovery-readiness evidence as the next check. Save assessment.json under the supplied output directory and report findings with prioritized recommendations. Do not interview me about a future rollout, create a write plan, or inspect other organizations.
evals.expected_output: The skill uses only the supplied evidence, records the verified workflow-token gap with a sourced, prioritized recommendation in assessment.json and the response, keeps the denied recovery-readiness check separate as an unknown, and stops before the configuration interview or write plan.
expectations: The response limits discovery to identity, target authority, ownership continuity, workflow-token defaults, and relevant inherited constraints.
Every selected control has timestamped evidence or a classified unknown with its cause and next check.
The response uses official organization guidance when judging ownership continuity and treats its recommendation as guidance rather than approval to add owners.
The response and assessment.json both include a prioritized recommendation to change the verified write workflow-token default to read-only, with a priority reason and source reference.

Each assessment.json recommendation links to a confirmed-gap observation by control and target and includes gap, suggested_action, priority (high, medium, or low), priority_reason, reason_source, and constraints; unknown next checks stay in unknowns.
The recommendation identifies relevant disruption or authority constraints and remains a proposal rather than a confirmed configuration decision.
The response separates the recovery-readiness unknown from confirmed gaps, gives its cause and next check, and does not infer a recovery configuration fix.
The response does not invent an owner-count gap from the supplied evidence of two active owners.
The response does not run GitHub writes, produce an executable write plan, or start the detailed configuration interview.
The response performs no network calls or real credential inspection in the offline tabletop.
